title: Review: The Game Store Report
explanation: Level 4 review! You now have a little connected database: players buy games in the sales table, and each game comes from a studio. Your job is to answer real business questions by joining them. Use INNER JOIN when you only want matches, and LEFT JOIN when you need to find what's missing. Tip: before writing, trace the chain of IDs you need to follow.

example.code:
SELECT g.title, st.studio_name
FROM games AS g
INNER JOIN studios AS st
  ON g.studio_id = st.studio_id
WHERE g.price = 0;

lines.explain: Show the game title and its studio.

tasks.prompt: Find the players who have never bought a game. Show just their username.
tasks.answer: SELECT p.username FROM players AS p LEFT JOIN sales AS sa ON p.player_id = sa.player_id WHERE sa.sale_id IS NULL;
hints: This is the 'finding what's missing' trick from Lesson 15: LEFT JOIN, then IS NULL.
FROM players AS p LEFT JOIN sales AS sa ON p.player_id = sa.player_id WHERE sa.sale_id IS NULL

solution_lines.explain: Show the username.
Start with ALL players.
Glue on sales, keeping players with no purchases.
Match each player to their sales.
Keep only players with no matching sale.

tasks.prompt: Find the games that have never been sold. Show just the title.
tasks.answer: SELECT g.title FROM games AS g LEFT JOIN sales AS sa ON g.game_id = sa.game_id WHERE sa.sale_id IS NULL;
hints: Same trick as task 1, but start from games this time.
FROM games AS g LEFT JOIN sales AS sa ON g.game_id = sa.game_id WHERE sa.sale_id IS NULL

solution_lines.explain: Show the game title.
Start with ALL games.
Glue on sales, keeping games that were never sold.
Match each game to its sales.
Keep only games with no sales.

tasks.prompt: Show the title of every game sold more than once, and how many times it sold (call it times_sold), most sold first.
tasks.answer: SELECT g.title, COUNT(sa.sale_id) AS times_sold FROM games AS g INNER JOIN sales AS sa ON g.game_id = sa.game_id GROUP BY g.title HAVING COUNT(sa.sale_id) > 1 ORDER BY times_sold DESC;
hints: Join games to sales, group by title, then filter the groups with HAVING.
... GROUP BY g.title HAVING COUNT(sa.sale_id) > 1 ORDER BY times_sold DESC

solution_lines.explain: Show each game and how many sales it has.
Start with games.

solution_lines.line: INNER JOIN sales AS sa ON g.game_id = sa.game_id
solution_lines.explain: Glue on sales.
Make one group per game.
Only keep games sold more than once.
Sort, most sold first.

tasks.prompt: For each player country, show the total money spent, rounded to 2 decimals (call it total_spent), biggest first.
tasks.answer: SELECT p.country, ROUND(SUM(g.price), 2) AS total_spent FROM sales AS sa INNER JOIN players AS p ON sa.player_id = p.player_id INNER JOIN games AS g ON sa.game_id = g.game_id GROUP BY p.country ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
hints: You need three tables: sales, players (for the country), and games (for the price).
... GROUP BY p.country ORDER BY total_spent DESC

solution_lines.explain: Show each country and the total spent there.
Start with sales.

solution_lines.line: INNER JOIN players AS p ON sa.player_id = p.player_id
solution_lines.explain: Bring in the buyer, who has the country.

solution_lines.line: INNER JOIN games AS g ON sa.game_id = g.game_id
solution_lines.explain: Bring in the game, which has the price.
Make one group per country.
Sort, biggest total first.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many rows will this return?
tasks.code:
SELECT DISTINCT st.studio_name
FROM sales AS sa
INNER JOIN games AS g
  ON sa.game_id = g.game_id
INNER JOIN studios AS st
  ON g.studio_id = st.studio_id;
hints: This finds which studios have at least one sale. DISTINCT removes repeats.
Nintendo and Rockstar each have 2 sales, and FromSoftware has 3, but each studio only counts once.

solution_lines.explain: Show each studio name once.
Start with all 13 sales.

solution_lines.line: INNER JOIN games AS g ON sa.game_id = g.game_id
solution_lines.explain: Find the game for each sale.

solution_lines.line: INNER JOIN studios AS st ON g.studio_id = st.studio_id;
solution_lines.explain: Find the studio for each game. After removing repeats, 8 different studios made a sale.

recap: Level 4 complete! You can now connect tables, chain joins, and find what's missing. That's how real company databases work.
